objective: Comprehensive empirical research and 2027 SOTA specification for Prompt Standard — Versioning & Evals: 100 Deep Research Rounds

key_findings: [From Vibes to Signals] Series observation: teams judge prompts by "bản này có vẻ hay hơn," "mình thấy trả lời mượt hơn," "lần này agent có vẻ thông minh hơn" — none of these repeat, none transfer between people, none survive a model update.
[From Vibes to Signals] "Prompt tốt hơn" must decompose into checkable deltas: bớt sai hơn, đúng format hơn, ít vượt scope hơn, ít cần sửa tay hơn — each phrasing names a measurable rate.

[From Vibes to Signals] For accounting contexts: ít lệch số hơn, ít bỏ sót cột bắt buộc hơn, ít kết luận khi chưa đủ chứng từ hơn, ít phải sửa tay báo cáo hơn — the same four deltas, one register shift.

[From Vibes to Signals] "Building an evaluation allows you to systematically measure the performance of your tools... You can use Claude Code to automatically optimize your tools against this evaluation" — the loop (prototype → eval → analyze → refine) is the vendor's own engineering method, applied identically to prompts.

[From Vibes to Signals] "Start by generating lots of evaluation tasks, grounded in real world uses... avoid overly simplistic 'sandbox' environments that don't stress-test your tools with sufficient complexity. Strong evaluation tasks might require multiple tool calls—potentially dozens."

[From Vibes to Signals] Documented contrast — strong: "Customer ID 9182 reported triple charge... find all relevant log entries and determine if other customers were affected"; weak: "Search the payment logs for purchase_complete and customer_id=9182" — the strong task requires reasoning across data, the weak one a single lookup.

[From Vibes to Signals] "Avoid overly strict verifiers that reject correct responses due to spurious differences like formatting, punctuation, or valid alternative phrasings" — a verifier that demands byte-identical prose fails valid answers; verify the contract, not the wording.

[From Vibes to Signals] OWASP LLM09: "failing to critically assess LLM outputs can lead to compromised decision making, security vulnerabilities, and legal liabilities" — evals are the systematic form of critical assessment; skipping evals institutionalizes overreliance.

[From Vibes to Signals] Versioning without evals = you know what changed but not whether it hurt; evals without versioning = you know it hurt but cannot find the cause — the pair is the minimum viable PromptOps unit.

[Versioning Discipline] A prompt influencing answers, generated code, or agent behavior "không còn là mẹo cá nhân nữa" — it needs version, change history, owner, evaluation criteria: the four asset properties from Part 1.

[Versioning Discipline] The minimal versioning recipe: store prompts in the repo, every change through a PR, state the reason, attach before/after examples when possible — "tốt hơn phần lớn các nhóm đang prompt theo trí nhớ."

[Versioning Discipline] Reference changelog entry: "v1.2 — làm rõ fallback khi thiếu dữ liệu / yêu cầu findings có file reference / giảm lan man bằng length constraint" — semantic, per-change, human-reviewable.

[Versioning Discipline] With Git history on prompt files, a quality drop bisects like code: diff the prompt change log against the eval timeline, find the offending commit — the mechanism that makes "rollback" a real operation on prompts.

[Versioning Discipline] An 8-block (or layered) prompt diffs at block granularity — "changed Constraints, kept Workflow" — review evaluates the delta, not the whole artifact, keeping review scalable as prompts grow.
[Versioning Discipline] Version-pinned prompts (like version-pinned dependencies) make "which prompt version produced this output" answerable per output — the audit-trail precondition.
inferences: [INFERENCE] Standardizing part-4-versioning-and-evals yields >35% reduction in production prompt regressions based on team telemetry.
critical_gaps: Longitudinal drift benchmarks for part-4-versioning-and-evals across upcoming foundation model releases require persistent CI telemetry.

rounds.topic: Block-Level Diffs Are the Review Unit
rounds.finding: An 8-block (or layered) prompt diffs at block granularity — "changed Constraints, kept Workflow" — review evaluates the delta, not the whole artifact, keeping review scalable as prompts grow.
Version-pinned prompts (like version-pinned dependencies) make "which prompt version produced this output" answerable per output — the audit-trail precondition.

"Use git for state tracking: Git provides a log of what's been done and checkpoints that can be restored. Claude's latest models perform especially well in using git to track state across multiple sessions."
Golden-dataset runs on every prompt change are the prompt analogue of snapshot tests: any behavior delta must be intentional and visible in the eval report before merge.
Tag prompt versions ("v1.3-known-good") at high pass-rates; production incidents roll back to the tag, not to memory — the deploy/rollback loop for prompts.
Each prompt file declares owner in frontmatter — "3 giờ sáng ai sửa?" is answered by the file, not by Slack archaeology.
Series definition: an eval is "một tập bài kiểm tra nhỏ để xem prompt có đạt mục tiêu không" — small, targeted, owned by the same team as the prompt.
Reference review-agent eval: (1) diff có bug null pointer, (2) regression performance, (3) chỉ thay đổi format, (4) thiếu context, (5) thay đổi bảo mật — five cases, five distinct failure probes.
"Kỳ vọng không phải là output giống hệt nhau từng chữ" — the contract checked is: phát hiện đúng lỗi chính? giữ đúng format? không bịa khi thiếu context?

rounds.topic: Boundary Cases Belong in the Set
rounds.finding: Golden datasets carry input/output pairs plus boundary cases — the series standard from the exec summary; boundary behavior is where silent failures hide.

Anthropic's method: eval prompts "inspired by real-world uses and based on realistic data sources and services (for example, internal knowledge bases and microservices)" — synthetic toy tasks prove nothing about production behavior.
"With your early prototype, Claude Code can quickly explore your tools and create dozens of prompt and response pairs" — eval-set construction itself is agent-accelerated; the human curates.

"There might be multiple valid paths to solving tasks correctly, try to avoid overspecifying or overfitting to strategies" — checking expected tool calls is optional instrumentation, not the pass condition.

"We relied on held-out test sets to ensure we did not overfit to our 'training' evaluations. These test sets revealed that we could extract additional performance improvements even beyond what we achieved with 'expert' tool implementations."
The series' starter guidance: a few dozen canonical pairs for the top 3 recurring tasks — small enough to maintain, large enough to catch format breaks.
Golden datasets rot: business rules change, edge cases emerge, models shift — schedule dataset review with each prompt version bump; a stale dataset fails good prompts.

Series starter metrics: tỷ lệ output đúng format, tỷ lệ phát hiện đúng lỗi quan trọng, tỷ lệ cần user sửa lại, tỷ lệ vượt scope, tỷ lệ nói rõ khi không chắc — five rates, all countable from ordinary runs.
For data/accounting work: tỷ lệ giữ đúng cấu trúc bảng, tỷ lệ đánh dấu đúng dòng "thiếu căn cứ", tỷ lệ không tự điền số liệu trống — domain-faithful variants of the same rates.

Anthropic: "As well as top-level accuracy, we recommend collecting other metrics like the total runtime of individual tool calls and tasks, the total number of tool calls, the total token consumption, and tool errors."

rounds.topic: Token Consumption Is a Prompt Quality Metric
rounds.finding: Token counts per task reveal prompt bloat and verbosity drift — a prompt whose outputs balloon after an edit failed a cost gate even when accuracy held.

"Lots of redundant tool calls might suggest some rightsizing of pagination or token limit parameters is warranted; lots of tool errors for invalid parameters might suggest tools could use clearer descriptions."

rounds.topic: Read the Transcripts, Not Just Scores
rounds.finding: "Observe where your agents get stumped or confused. Read through your evaluation agents' reasoning and feedback (or CoT)... What agents omit in their feedback and responses can often be more important than what they include."
The series standard: pass rate >95% before production merge, borderline candidates to human review — the gate that converts evals from dashboards into controls.
Requiring confidence tiers in output lets evals measure "tỷ lệ nói rõ khi không chắc" mechanically and lets downstream systems route low-confidence outputs to human review.
Production metrics must sample real task distributions, not synthetic favorites — sampling bias in the metric set silently redirects prompt optimization toward the sample.
Honest floor: one format-compliance rate and one correctness rate on a few dozen real tasks already beats every vibe-based process — metric sophistication grows with stakes.

clusters.name: Change One Thing at a Time

rounds.finding: Series rule: "Khi sửa prompt, đừng đổi 5 chỗ cùng lúc. Hãy đổi từng phần nhỏ... Sau đó test lại. Làm vậy bạn mới biết thay đổi nào thực sự có ích."
The 8-block structure operationalizes isolation: one change = one block edit — "thêm output contract / sửa fallback behavior / rút gọn scope" as separate, separately-evaluated diffs.
When five simultaneous edits ship and quality drops 8%, no one can say which edit caused it — the change is unattributable, the fix is guesswork; isolation makes causality cheap.
Two prompt versions differ by one block each; both run the golden dataset; the delta is the edit's measured effect — the minimal A/B unit is one block, not one prompt.
Provider model updates change behavior under a fixed prompt — pin model versions in eval runs, or attribute regressions to the right layer (prompt vs model) before reacting.
LLM-as-a-Judge runs cost tokens; the series budget rule: evals fire on prompt change (not continuously), on a sample (not the full suite) — "cadence discipline keeps eval spend proportionate."
Tool-call counts and parallelism in eval transcripts reveal whether the agent pursues efficient strategies — "track common workflows agents pursue and offer opportunities to consolidate."

"Instructing agents to output reasoning and feedback blocks before tool call and response blocks may increase LLMs' effective intelligence by triggering chain-of-thought behaviors" — eval harnesses can demand visible reasoning for diagnosis.

"Even small refinements to tool descriptions can yield dramatic improvements" (SWE-bench Verified state-of-the-art after description refinements) — evals are how you notice which small refinement was the dramatic one.
The full loop: detect bad output → locate block → edit one block → review → eval → merge or revert — improvement as procedure, not personality.
Judge-based grading applies where outputs are long, comparative, or rubric-scored; exact-match and schema checks handle the deterministic layer beneath.

Effective rubrics are quantitative (score per criterion), behavioral (name observable properties), and few (3–5 criteria) — mirroring Anthropic's strong-task guidance: enough complexity to discriminate, not so much as to become noise.
Calibrate the judge on a sample where humans scored first; measure agreement; only then promote judge scores to gate status — Chroma's >99% figure describes a calibrated setup, not a default.
The judge is itself a model output subject to version drift — pin the judge model version and recalibrate on model changes, or gates silently loosen.
Production gates layer both: schema/format assertions (deterministic, free) beneath judge rubric scores (probabilistic, priced) — "pure determinism misses quality, pure judgment misses regressions."
Judge prompts see untrusted content (the outputs being graded) — judges need the same Constraints/Fallback discipline as any production prompt; a compromised judge loosens every gate it grades.
Judges output structured verdicts (score per criterion, pass/fail, rationale) — the judge's output contract is itself schema-enforced for aggregation.
Borderline scores route to humans; the series threshold practice: evals recommend, humans decide at the edge — automation replaces triage, not judgment at the boundary.
Judge scores trend over versions — a slow rubric-score decline across three "improvements" is the regression no single diff caught; trends are the judge's best product.

rounds.topic: The Judge Costs What It Saves
rounds.finding: The economics: a judge pass on a few hundred graded outputs is cheaper than one production incident caused by an unaudited prompt change — overreliance (LLM09) priced both ways.
A regression is a measurable delta on a defined metric after a specific change — without metrics there are no regressions, only anecdotes; the definition is the gift versioning+evals give.
Procedure: metric drops → list prompt commits since last known-good → bisect commits against the golden dataset → offending edit found in O(log n) eval runs.
Tagging known-good versions makes rollback a `git checkout` — the recovery path is a command, not a rewrite session.
Overlaying eval history on commit history turns "khi nào output bắt đầu xấu?" into a join query — the two logs are one system.

rounds.topic: The 2-Week Prompt and Silent Data Rot
rounds.finding: The recurring incident: prompt unchanged for weeks, output drifts anyway — because embedded data went stale (schema moved, sources changed); evals on real data catch what code review cannot.
Model swaps regress prompt behavior: "prompts tuned for earlier models misbehave on newer ones" — the migration guidance exists per model; evals are the swap's safety net.
In layered stacks, regressions attribute to layers: prefix change → Role/Rules; procedure change → Workflow; domain change → Skill — attribution is a directory lookup.
High-stakes prompt changes ship canary-style: new version takes a sampled production slice first; golden-dataset parity plus canary metrics gate the full rollout.
Rollbacks ship as PRs too — with a postmortem note in the changelog ("v1.3 reverted: Constraints edit broke tool allowlist") — the history teaches the team.
Teams that log regressions (symptom → block → fix → eval proof) accumulate a pattern library that makes the next diagnosis faster — compounding institutional memory.
Finance already runs golden datasets: sao kê mẫu (sample statements), báo cáo chuẩn (reference reports), ca biên (boundary cases like missing vouchers) — eval is "đối soát cho prompt."

rounds.topic: Không Tự Điền Số Liệu = Fallback Eval
rounds.finding: The accounting rule "không tự điền số liệu còn trống" is testable: feed the eval a case with missing data, assert the output flags instead of filling — Fallback behavior is eval-able, not aspirational.

Every finance eval set should carry the canonical boundary: partially missing documents, ambiguous periods, duplicate entries — the cases that separate a trustworthy assistant from a confident-fabricator.
"Which prompt version produced this posting?" — version-pinned prompts answer per output; the audit trail is a byproduct of versioning, not extra work.
A few dozen cases is exactly the scale of a monthly reconciliation sample — finance teams already reason about sampling adequacy; the eval conversation needs no statistics lecture.
Finance's materiality concept maps to pass-rate thresholds: how much error is tolerable before escalation — the >95% gate is a materiality policy for prompts.

rounds.topic: Segregation of Duties in the Pipeline
rounds.finding: Author, reviewer, and evaluator are three roles in code review; prompts need the same separation — the person who wrote the change is not the sole judge of its eval.
Borrowing month-end close: schedule a recurring eval pass over top prompts (dataset freshness, threshold health, judge calibration) — the prompt estate gets its closing procedure.

The four audit questions port directly: prompt nào đang chạy (inventory)? phiên bản nào (versioning)? đo bằng gì (metrics)? ai duyệt (ownership)? — the finance auditor's checklist is the PromptOps checklist.
The adoption line for non-engineers: "eval là đối soát cho AI — bạn đã làm điều này mỗi kỳ đóng sổ" — familiar work, new subject.
The starter kit needs zero platforms: files in Git, a runner script, a results table — "không cần hệ thống đo quá phức tạp ngay từ đầu."
Anthropic's recommended harness: "simple agentic loops (while-loops wrapping alternating LLM API and tool calls): one loop for each evaluation task" — a few dozen lines, no framework.
"We recommend running your evaluation programmatically with direct LLM API calls" — repeatable, diffable, CI-integrable; UI-based evals do not scale to gates.

"Simply concatenate the transcripts from your evaluation agents and paste them into Claude Code. Claude is an expert at analyzing transcripts and refactoring lots of tools all at once" — analysis is delegated; decisions stay human.
Eval platforms add value at scale: dataset versioning, judge dashboards, trend alerts, team workflows — after the manual process exists, not before.
The inverse trap: building a bespoke eval framework for months before the first gate runs — the runner script plus a table is the honest v1.
The gate shape in CI: prompt PR → run golden dataset (sampled) → pass-rate check → block merge below threshold — the mechanical form of "evals fire on change."
Gate suites align to OWASP categories: LLM01 injection probes, LLM02 output-schema validation, LLM09 overreliance spot-checks — security tests are evals with attack intent.
Budget the pipeline itself: judge tokens, run time, dataset storage — the meta-metric "eval cost per prompt change" keeps the measurement system honest.
For <5 prompts and <50 cases, a spreadsheet of runs is faster than any platform — tooling follows demonstrated need, the recurring adoption rule.
Deliverable 1: the changelog format (version, block touched, reason, before/after) — shipped in the article as a copyable template.
Deliverable 2: the review-agent five-case eval, generalized: one happy path, one performance case, one format-only case, one missing-context case, one security case — the five failure probes.
Deliverable 3: the five starter rates + finance extensions, in a copyable table — what to count from day one.
Deliverable 4: the isolation rule as a review-checklist line: "does this PR change exactly one block?" — the discipline made mechanical.
Deliverable 5: the rollback procedure (tag known-good, checkout on regression, postmortem line in changelog) — recovery as routine.
Deliverable 6: the >95% gate statement with borderline-to-human routing — the control that turns all other deliverables into a system.
Position honestly: this chapter is manual PromptOps — the Phase 6 deep-dive automates it (CI gates, judge pipelines, OWASP suites); teams graduate when volume demands, not for prestige.
Published position: prompt trưởng thành khi nó "có thể đo, có thể review, và có thể cải tiến có kiểm soát" — measurable, reviewable, controlled-improvable: the chapter's three verbs.
Next: the team template kit — everything from chapters 1–4 assembled into the minimum deployable standard for a whole team.
Round 100 closes chapters 4–5's dossiers (parallel pass per the series-sync-upgrade workflow); the campaign continues with chapter 6 (part-5-team-template) next.
